example_prompt: Notify me when a payment is successfully completed.

id.description: Session identifier, the one returned at creation.

status.description:
`PENDING`: created, not confirmed yet (customer on the page, OTP pending, redirection in progress).
`SUCCESS`: confirmed by the aggregator. `FAILED`: refused or failed at the operator, the customer can retry on the same session.
`CANCELLED`: cancelled, no longer payable. `REFUNDED`: refunded from the dashboard.

oneOf.description: Your own free-form data, returned in webhooks. Cartflox adds `source` (`checkout_session`, `widget`, `payment_link`...) and, when relevant, `description`, `success_url`, `cancel_url` and `idempotencyKey`.

livemode.description: `true` for a production object, `false` for a test object: created with a test key, or in a workspace not switched live yet. Verify webhook signatures with the secret key of the same mode.

gotchas: The signature header carries a timestamp and a v1 HMAC-SHA256 hex value computed over the timestamp, a dot, and the raw body with your secret key; verify that value before acting on the event.
Verify the signature over the raw request body exactly as received; re-serializing the parsed JSON will change the bytes and make verification fail.
Reject events whose timestamp is more than 5 minutes old, which protects against replayed requests.
The same event can be delivered more than once, so make fulfilment idempotent keyed on data.id and data.status, or on the delivery identifier.
Any 2xx response acknowledges the delivery, and your handler must answer within 10 seconds, so process the order after responding rather than before.

spans: `t=<timestamp>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 hex of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with your secret key>`.
Get the **raw** request body, exactly as received (not the JSON parsed and then re-serialized).
Reject if the timestamp is more than 5 minutes old (replay protection).
Handle it idempotently, keyed on `data.id` and `data.status`.
Any `2xx` acknowledges the delivery. Answer within 10 seconds and process afterwards.
